articles.title: England losing tennis courts as number of padel facilities rises exponentially
articles.summary: Country loses 200 tennis courts in three years, but they still outnumber padel facilities by a factor of 11 to one. England has lost almost 200 tennis courts in three years as padel facilities have grown nearly sixfold.
body: Guardian analysis of Sport England data found that the country has lost 183 tennis courts since 2023 – the first such decline since at least 2000. The data includes local authority and community-owned courts, privately run health facilities, schools and sports clubs.

The number of padel courts, meanwhile, has risen exponentially. There are now more than 2,200, up from 382 in 2023. Research from the Lawn Tennis Association (LTA) found that a million people were playing padel as of May this year, up from 860,000 at the end of 2025.

The rise in padel – played on courts about three-quarters the size of tennis ones – is partly down to its accessibility. It blends tennis-style rules and scoring with squash-inspired features, including the use of a back wall, and is considered easier to learn thanks to the smaller courts and underarm serves.

Bee Armstrong, a project manager in London, took up padel in 2023 after suffering a back injury while playing hockey. “Padel is a bit easier on the body,” she said. “It’s really growing now so more people are getting into it.

articles.title: Michigan deny minnows Western Michigan with controversial last-second Hail Mary
articles.summary: Underwood throws for for 47-yard winning score. Officials put one second back on clock after review. No 16 Wolverines survive in Whittingham debut. Given an unlikely second chance at a game-ending Hail Mary, Bryce Underwood connected with JJ Buchanan for a 47-yard touchdown pass that lifted No 16…
body: The Wolverines were 27-and-a-hakf-point favorites in coach Kyle Whittingham’s debut. The Broncos thought they’d secured a historic upset when Underwood’s first Hail Mary sailed out of bounds with the clock expired.

WMU players were already on the field celebrating when officials called for a review. TV replays showed the clock hitting zero before the ball hit the hands of a Western Michigan defender, but officials ruled there was a second still to play.
Underwood heaved another throw, and Buchanan leaped to snag it and came down with it in the end zone.

Western Michigan was threatening to hand Michigan perhaps its biggest upset since a season-opening loss to Appalachian State in 2007, when the Wolverines were 33-point favorites. The Broncos kicked four field goals and forced three turnovers, including a late fumble by Underwood.

articles.title: Dane Sweeny’s ‘career-changing’ US Open comes to an end – along with Australia’s singles hopes
articles.summary: Australian wildcard loses 6-4, 6-3, 6-3 to Luciano Darderi. Sweeney frustrated by loss but says he had ‘an amazing week’ Dane Sweeny’s gallant and “career-changing” US Open campaign has come to a frustrating end with a tough third-round loss to seeded Italian Luciano Darderi.
body: Sweeny complained of a hip injury during the 6-4, 6-3, 6-3 defeat to the world No 22 that left Australia without a second-week singles hope in New York for the first time in five years.
Alex de Minaur’s shock second-round loss to Botic van de Zandschulp had left Sweeny as Australia’s last man standing at Flushing Meadows.
“It’s been an amazing week, a career-changing week, but I can’t help but feel a bit disappointed just with today’s performance,” Sweeny said.
“I just wasn’t really feeling it, just not really feeling the timing and the rhythm as I have been. Just made a lot of cheap errors and that was quite frustrating.

articles.title: Taylor's 'dream ending to a dream career'
articles.summary: Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Irish icon Katie Taylor sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells at Dublin's towering Croke Park.
body: Katie Taylor addressed the Croke Park crowd as she paid tribute to her mother Bridget, but her extended family of 83,000 inside Croke Park and many more tuning in will have known this one was for them too.
Fairytale endings in boxing are a rarity, but Taylor is no ordinary fighter and her swansong proved as extraordinary as the fighter and person.

After 30 years lacing up the gloves, Taylor, 40, sails off into the sunset after the most perfect of farewells in front of 83,000 adoring fans at Dublin's iconic Croke Park, just three miles from the scene of her first official bout 25 years earlier.
The final act in the ring was to sweep past Flora Pili to cement her legacy in Ireland and beyond, bowing out as a three-time and two-weight undisputed champion.

articles.title: 'I don't really want to talk' - Fritz and Cobolli shocked as seeds tumble
articles.summary: Taylor Fritz and Flavio Cobolli lose in the third round as six top-10 seeds are knocked out of the men's singles in the first week at the US Open.
body: Taylor Fritz was unable to explain how he let a two-set lead slip against Argentina's Francisco Cerundolo as he became one of six top-10 seeds to be eliminated from the men's draw in the first week of the US Open.
The American ninth seed was in complete control and went an early break up in the third set, only for 24th seed Cerundolo to produce a shock 3-6 4-6 6-3 6-4 6-4 win to reach the fourth round.
Less than an hour later, fifth seed Flavio Cobolli of Italy fell to a 6-7 (4-7) 6-3 6-0 6-3 defeat by Belgium's Alexander Blockx, opening up the men's draw even further.
However, German top seed Alexander Zverev did survive. The French Open champion won 6-2 7-6 (7-2) 6-2 against Chilean 25th seed Alejandro Tabilo to move into the last 16.

articles.title: 'The highlight of my whole career' - Taylor ecstatic with Croke Park swansong
articles.summary: Katie Taylor acclaimed becoming a three-time undisputed world champion in her farewell fight at Croke Park as the most special moment of her decorated career.
body: Katie Taylor beats Flora Pili in the final fight of her boxing career, becoming an undisputed world champion for the third time; the judges score it 100-90, 100-90, 98-91 as Taylor headlines first boxing event at Croke Park since Muhammad Ali fought Al “Blue” Lewis in 1972.
Taylor outclassed Flora Pili in a unanimous points victory in front of a crowd of 80,000 to ensure her three decades as an amateur and professional boxer ended in fairytale fashion.
Wild celebrations followed the announcement that she had overwhelmed the previously unbeaten Pili 100-90 100-90 98-91 on the scorecards.
For Taylor the feeling of signing off in front of her fans bettered winning Olympic gold at London 2012, headlining Madison Square Garden and her trilogy against Amanda Serrano.

articles.title: Can Lando Norris Win 3 in a Row?
articles.summary: The final lap of the Dutch Grand Prix came fast. After 72 laps, reigning world champion Lando Norris took the checkered flag and secured the final victory at the Zandvoort track. Norris’s title-defending season has been anything but impressive.
body: However, his season is turning around. After four podiums, he got his first win as a world champion during the Hungarian Grand Prix. He went into the summer break with a win, and came out of the summer break with a win.

For the Hungarian and Dutch Grand Prix, McLaren brought upgrades that have proven to be beneficial. Both drivers are finding their pace, and if these upgrades continue to work, both drivers could secure podiums and steal points for the Constructor’s championship.

The Italian Grand Prix at the Monza circuit is a test for McLaren. It’s rumored that they’ll be bringing their rotating wing, which Ferrari has used in the past and has brought them an advantage. Some other upgrades they’ve had include a new floor, wakeboards and floor slots, an engine cover, diffuser tweaks, and new front wheel rims.

Points-wise, Lando is only 24 behind Hamilton and Russell, and 83 points behind Antonelli. This weekend, Antonelli has to start from the back up the grid due to a new power unit. With Antonelli at the back, and if Norris can secure a solid qualifying position, Norris can significantly cut Antonelli’s lead.

articles.title: Gauff progresses at US Open, compatriots Fritz, Anisimova, Keys knocked out
articles.summary: Coco Gauff ensured the watching American public had something to cheer at the US Open as she progressed to the fourth round on a day when Taylor Fritz, Amanda Anisimova and Madison Keys suffered shock defeats.
body: Gauff, US Open champion in 2023, was facing world No 40 Cristina Bucsa, and though far from her best, did enough to grind out a 6-3 6-4 success to progress to the last 16.
The 22-year-old will next face compatriot Iva Jovic for a quarter-final spot.
"I think it was way different playing in the day than at night. Once I was down that break I just told myself I need to accelerate through my shots," Gauff said.
"She's a tricky player and sometimes she can pick it up and slow it down, so it was tough for me to get a rhythm but I'm just happy with how I fought through even when I wasn't playing my best."
